intro.heading: The festival of lights returns to the Atomium
body: For ten years the Brussels Diwali Festival has filled the esplanade of the Atomium with music, dance, food and light. It is the largest celebration of Diwali in Belgium.

The tenth edition carries the theme Culture United. For the first time, European embassies and cultural institutes join us, each pairing a tradition of their own with an Indian one, along an avenue of lights running the length of the esplanade.

highlights.title: From €10
highlights.text: Tickets go on sale 1 September. €10 until 30 September, €12 from 1 October, €15 at the gate. Children under 12 come free, but they still need an event band, so register them with the rest of your booking.

highlights.title: Culture United
highlights.text: European embassies and cultural institutes celebrate alongside us, each bringing a tradition of their own.

highlights.title: Forty kitchens
highlights.text: Regional cooking from across India, a bazaar of crafts and textiles, and bars along the esplanade. Card only, no cash.

highlights.title: Two stages
highlights.text: Classical and contemporary Indian music, dance from across the subcontinent, and fireworks at nine each evening.

practical.a: Heysel / Heizel on metro line 6, two minutes from the esplanade. Tram 7 and 51 stop nearby. Parking C is a short walk. We would rather you came by metro, the site fills quickly and parking does not.
Every bar and kitchen on site takes card and contactless only. There is no cash on the esplanade and no cash machine. Bring a card or your phone.

Children under 12 come free, but they still need an event band. Register them with the rest of your booking and give their date of birth, so we know how many people are on site. Everyone is given an event band at the gate, adults included. The date of birth is used only to check age and to count numbers on site, and it is deleted after the festival. There is a children's area with workshops and storytelling.
The festival goes ahead in any weather, stages are covered and much of the food is under canvas. Tickets are not refundable for rain. Bring a coat; Brussels in October is Brussels in October.

The esplanade is flat and step-free throughout. Accessible toilets are next to the main stage. If you are coming with a wheelchair or need assistance, write to us beforehand and we will make sure someone meets you at the gate.

panels.a: For the tenth edition we have invited European embassies and cultural institutes to celebrate alongside us. Each brings a tradition of their own and pairs it with an Indian one: a duet, a shared dish, a dance answered by another dance. Diwali is a festival of light, and light is not the property of one country.
A path of lamps runs the length of the esplanade, from the Heysel metro to the foot of the Atomium, each stretch given to a participating country. It is lit from dusk on both evenings.

The first Brussels Diwali was held in 2016. Since 2017 it has taken place on the esplanade of the Atomium, growing from a community gathering into the largest celebration of Diwali in Belgium, and one that is now as Belgian as it is Indian.
